title: Doubled pawns
line: Two pawns on one file: when they hurt and when they do not.

steps.text: Take the knight with your bishop. Black takes back with a pawn.
steps.after: Black takes back with the pawn from d7. That opens lines for its queen and bishop.

steps.text: Two pawns of one side on the same file are doubled pawns. Tap Black's doubled pawns.
steps.hint: Look along the files on the side where the knight was taken.
steps.after: The back one is stuck behind the front one and cannot move past it.

steps.text: With queens and pieces on, they cost Black little: Black has both bishops and its pieces come out fast.
With every piece traded, they hurt. White has four pawns against three on the right. Black's extra pawn on the left is the doubled one.
Push your extra pawn. Four pawns against three can make a pawn no black pawn can stop. Black's extra pawn is stuck behind another.
steps.hint: It is the pawn in front of your king.
steps.after: Black's king comes to stop it.

steps.text: Bring your king up behind your pawns.
steps.after: Black pushes on the left, but its back pawn there still has a pawn of its own in front of it.

summary: Doubled pawns are often fine while pieces are on. In an ending they make it hard to get a pawn through.
